correctness.rationale: The proof establishes labeled simplicity probability using exact nonsingular-matrix count and directed cut bounds; reconstructs the complete monomial action on simple matrices; bounds all nonidentity diagonal and moving-permutation Burnside terms by explicit R_{n,q}; proves R_{n,q}->0 for every fixed q>=3; and derives the isomorphism class and generic-rigidity conclusions. Exhaustive independent orbit/stabilizer/Burnside calculations for q=2,3,5 in small dimensions matched the theoretical identities. Finite tests do not establish the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: The fixed-field q >=3 simple orbit asymptotic and conditional trivial-automorphism law were not stated in the inspected 2023 Burnside framework or the 2026 survey; the latter explicitly lists random and counting asymptotics as questions. An earlier binary-field quantitative symmetry result and a general labeled simplicity-probability estimate are acknowledged and excluded from priority claims. The new argument bounds weighted monomial stabilizers and turns labeled counts into simple isomorphism-class asymptotics. Searches did not establish uniqueness and an undiscovered older asymptotic is a residual risk.

value.rationale: The leading-order census of simple isomorphism types over fixed q>=3 answers a natural, explicitly motivated restricted version of the 2026 open asymptotic counting question and distinguishes labeled matrix probabilities from isomorphism orbit counts. The generic-triviality theorem controls otherwise potentially dominant scalar and permutation stabilizers and is necessary for the counting asymptotic. It is a meaningful structural/probabilistic classification fact, not an arbitrary finite calculation.
